# Downstream SolidCore changes

`face37.patch` changes the implementation of planar Face 37 (hole-loop nesting) in the pinned SolidCore revision. The public kernel check level and tolerances are unchanged. The patch and the original/patched file hashes are in [the lock file](../solidcore.lock.json). The local vendor tool and native Linux image both verify the patch before compiling it.

For a planar face with at least four loops, the check builds each inner loop's UV control-polygon bounds at most once. A B-spline on its natural knot interval with positive finite rational weights lies inside its Euclidean control hull. The winding of such a loop cannot put a point strictly outside the expanded hull inside the loop. Only the inner-versus-inner **Inside** predicate uses this exclusion. The outer-loop classification is unchanged. Unknown or missing trims, an edge interval extending beyond the curve's domain, nonpositive or nonfinite weights, non-planar faces, and points near or inside the expanded bounds all use the upstream classifier. Every loop still participates in Level‑1.

This replaces expensive distant pair classifications with cheap comparisons; it does **not** make the pair enumeration subquadratic. Independent checks on the face, surface, edge, vertex and topology still run, including the manifold and mass-property checks in Colocad. See [the native negative regression](../../crates/agent-cad/tests/level1_nesting.rs).

`validation-properties.patch` accelerates the minimum-speed and minimum-curvature-radius tests on spline trims. It is enabled when Colocad inspects terminal bodies in plain assemblies. A clamped rational quadratic curve qualifies only if each knot span is a quadratic Bézier span, its positive weights and coordinate range satisfy the numerical guards, and a conservative lower bound exceeds the native threshold by a factor of eight. The code bounds the derivative using its Bernstein poles. It bounds curvature radius using speed squared divided by an upper bound on acceleration. The checks use one-sided bounds at knots. Existing knot, continuity, topology and manifold checks still execute. With only this base patch, mapped trim curvature uses its original solver; the metric-specific extension below is separate. Ambiguous spans and the stricter solver-status policy also retain the generic path.

The same patch can reuse a completed pure spline solve for bit-identical poles, knots, curve flags, interval, property and separation. Changes to kernel settings invalidate the cache. The cache stores successful results with at most 16 solution ends and caps key and value payload at 1 MiB and 512 entries per kernel. Cancellable operations bypass both shortcuts. [Comparison against native failure reports](../../crates/agent-cad/tests/validation_properties.rs)

`planar-conic-domain.patch` supplements sampled planar STEP parameter boxes with the stationary points of each bounded Circle/Ellipse projected onto the plane's U/V axes. A projection is `A cos(t) + B sin(t)`; its derivative zeros recur every 180 degrees. The mapper restricts conic edge spans to at most one turn, so at most three stationary candidates per axis cover either edge sense, including a wrapped interval. A constant projection adds no candidates. Existing samples and bounds remain; no curve, topology, tolerance, assertion or error policy is changed. Non-planar surfaces, Lines and B-splines retain their previous path; this is **not** a general B-spline bound fix.

The patch addresses an underestimated sampled domain that can send a planar rational-curve drop through clamping/fallback and lose an arc segment. Synthetic continuous-extrema, reversed interval, tilted plane, wrap, full turn and degenerate-projection cases are in `step_planar_conic_domain.rs`. A corrupted UV trim must still trigger the existing loop-gap check. The G3-B long-arc source is a private cross-check only: same mechanism and coverage remain unconfirmed until a fresh first-check Windows receipt. All runtime validation for this candidate is Windows/WSL2-only and currently pending.

The closed-solid delivery control in `step_planar_conic_delivery.rs` rotates the seam of the public drilled-block fixture by 17 degrees together with both circular edges, cylindrical reference frame, corresponding plane pcurves, vertices and seam line. It exercises native import/build/export/readback and a deliberately inconsistent seam-vertex negative. This is a full-delivery non-regression control; it is not required to fail before the patch because the outer rectangular face already bounds the bore. Independent Windows OCP material comparisons remain unknown until actual receipts. No generated fixture, local geometry execution or G1 workaround is part of this candidate.

`periodic-seam-trims.patch` aligns a STEP cylinder’s analytic support with its finite face parameter window before constructing edge trims. It keeps the source geometry and existing validation tolerances. The synthetic annulus regression verifies cyclic loop starts, equivalent loop directions, a through-hole, mass properties and rejection of an off-curve vertex. Remove the patch when the pinned STEP bridge derives the same bounded cylinder domain.

The spline validation overlay also reports raw and tolerance-grouped endpoint knot multiplicities, along with curve dimension and degree, when the current endpoint check fails. The predicate is unchanged.

`step-brep-end-poles.patch` removes a redundant endpoint knot and its zero-support pole when canonical reconstruction over-clamps a previously clamped STEP edge. The shared edge constructor applies the same correction before both topology-first and stitched face reconstruction. Remaining poles, weights and parameter values are unchanged. Remove the patch when the pinned STEP bridge preserves endpoint multiplicity in this import path.
`uv-metric-regularity.patch` applies that existing certificate to the actual metric-mapped trim. The original UV certificate continues to govern the original first-derivative check; it is never reused as a certificate of the mapped curvature. The mapped curve must independently satisfy the original positive-weight, finite-coordinate, knot-span, projection-roundoff and eight-times-threshold guards, using the unchanged mapped tolerance. If sizing or certification fails, or cancellation/strict status/zero-speed-end policies require it, the original solver remains. Knot, internal-control-point, topology and manifold checks still execute. An exact identity metric reuses the source trim and its existing bounding box for the radius check and never allocates a mapped clone. Mapped-trim sizing and mapped regularity live in a non-inlined helper so identity and analytic validation do not keep that TEXT in the main check CGU; `quadratic_regularity` is not called on a mapped clone when mapping produced `None`. The coincident-pole check also uses the source trim directly for identity metrics. Non-identity metrics still use the mapped control net.

The vendor verifier accepts a prepared sequence only when every patched target matches its final hash in the trusted lock, in addition to the archive, patch and whole-tree checks. This permits repeated builds when a later patch modifies an earlier target. A forged local manifest cannot grant a different patched-target hash. The public synthetic [patch-chain regression](../../test/vendor-patches.test.mjs) checks this case and target, patch and archive tampering.
`step-spherical-face-sense.patch` maps native spherical and conical normal
reversals (`swap_uv ^ inside_out`, const surface flags only) to STEP
`ADVANCED_FACE.same_sense` in a non-inlined helper. A single shell, or every
shell of one material solid (outer plus enclosed voids), owns the face/edge/
vertex tables by move. Compound B-reps keep one body per shell so product
assemblies stay separate solids. STEP sphere frames and pcurves already use
the outward analytic parameterization. The patch preserves the edge loops,
geometric tolerances and import checks. Remove it when the pinned STEP
bridge carries the same correction.
[Native exchange regressions](../../crates/agent-cad/tests/step_spherical_face_sense.rs)
cover ordinary and reflected rounded solids and enclosed spherical trims.
